apps/web/modules/bookings/hooks/useOverl.label: fair
apps/web/modules/bookings/hooks/useOverl.reason: The description says the overlay 'starts with the calendars selected for conflict checking and loads them right away, instead of starting with the primary calendar only'. That gives: isSelected calendars toggled, primary not, and one onToggleCalendar call with {credentialId, externalId} entries (the base ToggledConnectedCalendars shape).

apps/web/modules/bookings/hooks/useOverl.label: ambiguous
apps/web/modules/bookings/hooks/useOverl.reason: Requires not initializing while connectedCalendars is [], then initializing on rerender. Base useOverlayCalendar treats [] as loaded (`connectedCalendars && ...`) and sets initalised. The description implies auto-loading after login but never mentions this existing empty-array bug, so keeping the base guard is a plausible reading.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/__.label: fair
packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/__.reason: Returns [] without calling events.list, the same early return as base getAvailability ('Early return if only other integrations are selected'). The eventsListMock comes from a hidden support file supplied at evaluation.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/__.label: unfair
packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/__.reason: A single toEqual fixes several details nothing in 1-3 determines: self-declined and transparent events are dropped, the all-day event becomes '2024-01-10T18:30:00.000Z' (midnight in the response's timeZone, then toISOString) while dateTime events pass through as raw '+05:30' strings, and the untitled event has no title. events.list with singleEvents:true and pageToken paging is a reasonable Google API choice, but the output encoding is invented.

packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib.label: ambiguous
packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib.reason: Free events filtered and the `${dateTime}Z` format follow base getAvailability, but the URL must contain exactly '$select=showAs,start,end,subject&'. Any field order is valid for Graph, and the spec doesn't give one.
packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib.clarification: getAvailabilityWithTitles requests the same calendarView URL as getAvailability with `subject` appended to the select list: `$select=showAs,start,end,subject&$top=999`.

packages/features/calendars/weeklyview/u.label: ambiguous
packages/features/calendars/weeklyview/u.reason: Not spilling into the next day is natural with an exclusive end, but the asserted segment end '2024-01-11 00:00' (next midnight rather than 23:59) is a representation choice the spec doesn't fix.
packages/features/calendars/weeklyview/u.clarification: A segment's end on a day the event runs past is the next day's midnight (dayStart.add(1, 'day')), not 23:59; an event ending exactly at midnight does not appear on the following day.

packages/features/calendars/weeklyview/u.label: ambiguous
packages/features/calendars/weeklyview/u.reason: A zero-length event at midnight must return [00:00, 00:00] for its own day and null for the previous day. A plain overlap test (start < dayEnd && end > dayStart) returns null, and dropping zero-length events is a valid choice the description doesn't rule out.

packages/features/calendars/weeklyview/u.label: fair
packages/features/calendars/weeklyview/u.reason: An event inside the day returns its own start and end, which follows from the function's documented purpose and return type.

packages/features/calendars/weeklyview/u.clarification: A segment's end on a day the event runs past is the next day's midnight (dayStart.add(1, 'day')), not 23:59; an event ending exactly at midnight does not appear on the following day.
